text: **A RETIRED SKILL IS GONE FROM EVERY LOCATION ITS LIFECYCLE TOUCHES, AND EACH MEASUREMENT BELOW NAMES THE VERSION IT IS TRUE OF** -- because in this estate a premise carries one, and a claim true of v2 reads identically after it stops being true of v3. **RETIREMENT IS A THREE-LOCATION OPERATION -- the canon source, the manifest entry, and the installed tree under `~/.claude/skills/` -- and deleting the canon file reaches only the first.** **MEASURED AGAINST v3** (`intentsvcs::payload` at HEAD, driven 2026-09-02 in a disposable tempdir fixture, install tree and Claude target and manifest all throwaway): install a skill, delete its canon source, run `sync`. Outcome `SourceMissing`, **the installed directory is still there, and the manifest entry is still there.** `sync` reports the orphan and prunes nothing. **ALSO v3, AND IT IS THE HALF THAT INVERTS THE SEVERITY: `Payload::sync` has exactly ONE caller in the whole CLI -- the explicit `skills sync` verb -- so nothing automatic ever runs it.** A canon-only delete strands the skill silently and indefinitely, while `~/.claude/skills/`, which is what Claude Code actually reads, goes on loading it into every session. **MEASURED AGAINST v2, AND STATED ONLY AS THE CONTRAST: `bin/intent_upgrade:202` runs `intent claude skills sync`, so under v2 the stranding was at least REPORTED on every upgrade.** That line is still present and still accurate, **and it is not a fact about the shipped tool** -- citing it as one is the defect this row was drafted with and corrected for. **REMOVAL IS MODELLED AND THE DELETE DOES NOT REACH IT**, which is what makes this a lifecycle finding rather than a gap: `Outcome::Removed { removed, left }` distinguishes files this tool wrote from files it never wrote and left alone. **That is `uninstall`'s verb.** Fail-forward: retired means gone, never deprecated in place. **SPLIT FROM `AC-00.4` 2026-09-02 (vc): the two were drafted as one row and are two subjects with two instruments -- `AC-00.4` is answered by asking who calls, this one by driving a lifecycle in a fixture.**
